analysis.summary: Opening Group A fixture between an in-form, settled South Korea and a Czechia side at their first World Cup since 2006 under Miroslav Koubek, who has coached only two competitive matches. Korea were AFC's only unbeaten qualifier and won both US warm-ups; Czechia reached the finals via back-to-back playoff penalty shootouts and rely heavily on set pieces and crosses to Patrik Schick. Altitude in Guadalajara (~1,560 m) is expected to favour Korea, who have been training at altitude while Czechia prepared in Dallas. A tight, low-scoring game is the most likely shape, with Korea's superior attacking talent against Czechia's dead-ball threat.
analysis.home_form: Unbeaten through AFC qualifying (topped groups in Rounds Two and Three, AFC's only undefeated side). Pre-tournament friendlies: 5-0 v Trinidad and Tobago (May 30, Son and Cho Gue-sung 2 each) and 1-0 v El Salvador (Jun 3, Lee Dong-gyeong free kick). Caveat: zero open-play goals across the March friendlies v Ivory Coast and Austria.
analysis.away_form: First World Cup since 2006. Qualified via UEFA playoffs, beating Republic of Ireland 4-3 and Denmark 3-1 on penalties. New coach Miroslav Koubek (appointed Dec 2025) has only two competitive matches in charge. June warm-ups: beat Kosovo 2-1 and Guatemala 3-1. Eight qualifying goals from set pieces, the most of any European nation.
analysis.h2h: Three previous meetings, all friendlies: Czechia won 5-0 in 2001; South Korea won the most recent meeting 2-1 on June 5, 2016. Never met at a World Cup.
injuries_news: South Korea: Cho Yu-min injured pre-camp, replaced by uncapped Cho Wi-je; Bae Jun-ho (ankle) questionable but not expected to start; Hwang In-beom was managing an ankle issue when called up (fitness unconfirmed).
Czechia: Jan Kuchta (ankle) may be limited to substitute duty; Adam Hlozek returning from a largely lost injury season; otherwise squad reported healthy.
Probable shapes: South Korea 3-4-2-1 with Son Heung-min, Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae; Czechia 3-4-3 with Matej Kovar in goal, Schick up front, Soucek and Krejci as set-piece threats.
key_factors: Altitude (~1,560 m): Korea trained at altitude in Guadalajara; Czechia arrive from Dallas at sea level — late-game fitness could favour Korea.
Czechia's set-piece and crossing game (Schick, Chory, Soucek) targets Korea's main vulnerability in defending dead balls.
Managerial mismatch: Hong Myung-bo's settled, long-prepared side versus Koubek with two competitive games in charge.
Likely final World Cup for Son Heung-min (33); Lee Kang-in is Korea's main creator.
Winner takes early control of Group A behind favourites Mexico, raising stakes for both sides; cagey opener likely.
